$comment: Frames as the real emitters actually produce them, kept in ONE file so the TypeScript (zod) and Python (pydantic) suites validate the same bytes. A sample that only one language checks is a sample that only proves one generator works. Provenance is on every entry, and it says which kind it is: most entries name the emitter and the line they were copied from, while a contract defined BEFORE its emitters exist (the plan channel) names the design instead. An entry whose `from` names no emitter is the shape the first emitter must be written to, not a shape observed on a wire -- said here so the difference is legible rather than inferred.

valid.from: scl3300-stream docs/PROTOCOL.md, Payloads > data (verbatim)

valid.from: same emitter, the sample-with-no-valid-angle case that must never render as 0

valid.from: same emitter, the deprecated dual-emit copy sent immediately after the frame above

valid.name: angle-stream-heartbeat
valid.from: needle-guide electron/modules/inclinationStreamServer.ts, heartbeatFrame()

valid.name: angle-stream-heartbeat-versioned
valid.from: the same heartbeat once the emitter reports its version on the tick (this package's addition)

valid.name: plan-channel-plan-request
valid.from: docs/decisions.md ADR-0003 — the plan channel's contract is defined before its emitters, so this is the frame needle-simulator's Stage 2 sender must produce, with every optional field present. The four plan numbers are the ones needle-guide's operator types into shared/planInputs.ts today.

valid.name: plan-channel-plan-request-minimal
valid.from: the same sender with only the required fields: a plan that constrains the tilt and nothing else is a complete plan, and an absent entry point must not read as 0 mm

valid.name: plan-channel-plan-request-at-the-limits
valid.from: the same sender at every bound needle-guide shared/planInputs.ts states — inclination 90 (horizontal), azimuth -180, entry lateral at MAX_ENTRY_LATERAL_MM and entry longitudinal at MAX_ENTRY_LONGITUDINAL_MM, which are no longer the same number. Inclusive on both sides there, so inclusive here; a bound that disagreed by one endpoint would refuse a plan the operator's own form accepted.

valid.name: plan-channel-plan-request-longitudinal-past-the-lateral-bound
valid.from: needle-guide issue #429 / PR #456 — the 2026-09-05 rehearsal, where a stored `entry_longitudinal_mm` past a metre made every arriving plan unusable. Pinned as its own entry because it is the case a single shared entry-offset bound got wrong: 2500 mm along the table is an ordinary position for a scanner whose travel runs past 1000 mm, while the same number across the patient (entry_lateral_mm) is refused. A sample that only sat inside both bounds could not tell the two apart.

valid.name: plan-channel-plan-ack-pending-confirm
valid.from: needle-guide's first answer to plan-channel-plan-request: the frame parsed, and it is now in front of an operator who has not pressed Apply. Same envelope `id`; `applied_revision` is the revision still in effect, which is the PREVIOUS one.

payload.reason: Waiting for the operator to press Apply.

valid.name: plan-channel-plan-ack-applied
valid.from: needle-guide's SECOND answer to the same request, minutes later, when the operator pressed Apply. Same envelope `id` as the pending_confirm above — one request, two acks — which is why a sender may not close the correlation on the first.

valid.name: plan-channel-plan-ack-rejected
valid.from: needle-guide dismissing a later revision: the plan is refused and the reason is the operator-facing line the sender shows verbatim. `applied_revision` says what the guide kept, so the sender renders the other screen rather than what it hoped.

valid.name: tracker-hello-v2
valid.from: needle-simulator packages/needle-jetson/.../server/websocket.py, _handler()

valid.name: tracker-hello-unknown-peer
valid.from: same emitter, the branch where remote_address is missing

valid.name: tracker-hello-additive-field
valid.from: a future rig: the tracker's own rule is that additive optional fields do NOT bump protocol_version, so this MUST parse

invalid.name: device-payload-belongs-to-another-type
invalid.why: A status payload under type:data. This is the case a naive allOf-if/then codegen accepts, which is why the envelopes are emitted as tagged unions.

invalid.name: device-legacy-ts-key
invalid.why: The pre-x-version-2.0.0 spelling of t_boot_ms. Rejected here on purpose: a host that reads a boot clock as wall-clock time is wrong by however long the device has been powered.

invalid.name: device-status-envelope-version-malformed
invalid.why: `envelope_schema_version` is the number that decides whether this host can read this device, so a two-part "2.0" is not a lenient spelling of 2.0.0 — it is a value no comparison can be trusted on. Rejecting it here is what keeps the pattern in the schema load-bearing rather than decorative.

invalid.name: angle-stream-theta-payload-on-inclination-frame
invalid.why: type:inclination carrying the legacy theta field. Accepting it would let a 90-degrees-off angle through wearing the canonical label.

invalid.name: angle-stream-angle-as-string
invalid.why: A present-but-not-a-number angle is a malformed frame, not an angle of zero.

invalid.name: angle-stream-missing-link
invalid.why: Without link the subscriber cannot tell an idle sensor from a dead cable, which is the whole reason the field is required.

invalid.name: angle-stream-unknown-frame-type
invalid.why: An unrecognised frame type has no payload contract, so nothing can be said about it.

invalid.name: plan-channel-inclination-out-of-range
invalid.why: 91 degrees from vertical is a needle pointing back out of the patient, and it is one degree outside the range needle-guide's own form accepts. REFUSE, NEVER CLAMP: silently moving it to 90 would apply a plan the operator never planned, and the operator would have no way to see that it had happened.

invalid.name: plan-channel-longitudinal-out-of-range
invalid.why: 3001 mm is one millimetre past MAX_ENTRY_LONGITUDINAL_MM, so the widened bound still has an edge and this pins where it is. The bound is there to catch garbage — a stray keystroke, a value typed in the wrong unit — not to encode a clinical limit, and the same REFUSE, NEVER CLAMP rule applies: an entry point quietly pulled back to 3000 would put the needle somewhere the operator never planned.

invalid.name: plan-channel-plan-missing-plan-id
invalid.why: Without plan_id nothing correlates this plan to the next revision of it, so the receiver cannot tell an update from a second plan and cannot be idempotent about either.

invalid.name: plan-channel-plan-unknown-payload-field
invalid.why: The one sample that pins additionalProperties:false on this contract, and the reason the plan channel is closed where the angle stream is open. A key the receiver does not understand is a part of the plan it would silently drop; half a plan applied is worse than no plan applied, so the frame is refused whole.

invalid.name: plan-channel-unknown-envelope-field
invalid.why: Same rule one level up. An envelope key nobody agreed on is a routing or priority instruction the receiver would ignore while answering as though it had honoured it.

invalid.name: plan-channel-angle-stream-frame-on-the-plan-port
invalid.why: `kind: "evt"` is the angle stream's envelope, which pins that const because it is OUTPUT ONLY (needle-guide SYSTEM_SPEC.md 5.3). This is what an operator who typed 8791 where they meant 8790 actually sends, and the two contracts must be unable to satisfy each other — otherwise a mis-typed port reaches a real server and looks healthy.

invalid.name: plan-channel-ack-wearing-a-request-kind
invalid.why: An ack labelled `kind: "req"`. The envelope binds kind to type in its allOf table for this: a receiver that dispatches on `type` alone would take an answer for a command, and a request/response channel where the two are interchangeable is not one.

invalid.name: plan-channel-ack-payload-on-a-plan-frame
invalid.why: An ack payload under type:plan. This is the case a naive allOf-if/then codegen accepts, which is why every envelope here is emitted as a tagged union — and a new contract that did not carry the sample would not be covering the bug.

invalid.name: plan-channel-inclination-as-string
invalid.why: A present-but-not-a-number angle is a malformed plan, not an angle. JSON has a real number type, so a quoted "22.5" is a sender bug, and coercing it here would turn that bug into a plausible plan.

invalid.name: plan-channel-ack-unknown-result
invalid.why: A result the sender has no branch for. `maybe` is not a weaker `applied`: the sender must not guess whether the plan is in effect, so an unrecognised result is refused rather than treated as one of the three.

invalid.name: tracker-hello-no-version
invalid.why: Without protocol_version the client cannot decide whether it can read the stream, and connecting anyway is how a v1 rig gets driven as a v2 one.

invalid.name: tracker-hello-version-as-string
invalid.why: A string version compares unequal to every supported integer, which would look like a protocol mismatch rather than a malformed hello.
